summary: Discovered one RECAP terminal-fragment candidate and saved candidate-discovery.json. Discovery only; no skill package was authored.

candidates.name: rdkit-recap-terminal-fragments
candidates.capability: Extract unique terminal molecular fragments using RDKit RecapDecompose and GetLeaves.
candidates.boundary: Valid RDKit molecules, optionally parsed from SMILES. Molecular fragmentation only; no descriptors, synthetic feasibility assessment, or scientific validation. Parsing failures must remain distinct from successful empty results.
candidates.value: Clarifies terminal versus intermediate fragments, SMILES-keyed uniqueness, dummy attachment markers, and valid empty output.
candidates.usage_path: In an already provisioned Docker container with Python and RDKit, parse with Chem.MolFromSmiles and reject failed parsing. Call root = Recap.RecapDecompose(mol), then leaves = root.GetLeaves(). Present sorted(leaves.keys()); access molecules through leaves[smi].mol. Preserve '*' markers. root.children contains immediate children; root.GetAllChildren() contains all descendants. GetLeaves excludes the root and returns {} when it has no children.
candidates.construction: Direct packaging of existing RDKit interfaces, source-linked interpretation, prerequisites, and examples. Any wrapper should provide only parsing, input checks, and serialization. No new fragmentation algorithm is needed. Future business execution must occur only in Docker.

evidence.claim: Inspected document.py lines 31-56: overview and example demonstrate MolFromSmiles -> RecapDecompose -> GetLeaves, distinguishing 4 immediate children, 5 descendants, and 3 terminal fragments; leaf.mol exposes the molecule.

Inspected document.py lines 97-118 and 134-138: GetLeaves traverses children and returns terminal nodes in a SMILES-keyed dictionary. A root without children returns {}; keys represent unique fragments, not occurrence counts.
Inspected document.py lines 146-213: RecapDecompose consumes a molecule, creates the hierarchy, and defaults to independent allNodes state. It provides no explicit malformed-input parsing contract.

Inspected document.py lines 180-195, 231-235, and 279-293: default filtering rejects certain small products; CCCOCCC validly has no children. With minFragmentSize=3, the test expects its unique leaf '*CCC'. Empty output therefore need not indicate invalid input.

Inspected document.py lines 63-86: dependencies include Chem and rdChemReactions; reaction definitions introduce '*' endpoints. Lines 81-82 identify an aromatic nitrogen–aromatic carbon rule as outside the standard RECAP set.

Inspected the entire document.txt license: BSD 3-Clause redistribution conditions require retained notices and disclaimers and restrict endorsement. document.py lines 1-29 additionally carry Novartis notices.

gaps: Runtime behavior and RDKit availability were not tested.
The supplied module does not specify malformed-SMILES, zero-atom, or disconnected-input policies; the author stage must explicitly define its input contract.
Docker prerequisites and RDKit version compatibility remain for author-stage verification.
